messages:
emma.design: Quick sweep request — observed weird tab order in the Metrics / Alerts list when keyboard navigating. Repro steps below. rachel.a11y: thanks — can you paste repro? which browser/sr? emma.design: Safari + VoiceOver, macOS 13.6. Steps: open console -> Dashboard -> Alerts tab -> press Tab repeatedly. Focus jumps Alert 1 title -> 'Create Alert' button -> Alert 3 action menu, skipping Alert 2 entirely. vik.engineering: hm that sounds like DOM reordering when hidden elements get tabindex=-1? I'll dig into the list rendering. emma.design: here's the fragment I suspect: ```
  • ...
    • ``` we render headers as separate elements, maybe they aren't grouped. rachel.a11y: two quick things: 1) list should use role="list" and all items role="listitem" and not rely on tabindex on listitem. 2) ensure interactive controls inside list items are reachable and that overall DOM order matches visual order. VoiceOver follows DOM order, not visual stacking. vik.engineering: agreed. In our virtualized list we recycle nodes which may change DOM order when items unmount — that could explain the jump. I'll try setting container to `aria-live="polite"`? Not sure that's right here. rachel.a11y: don't use aria-live to fix ordering. That changes announcements. Instead change virtualization to maintain stable DOM order or use `aria-posinset`/`aria-setsize` on listitems so SRs can understand positions. amanda.content: from copy side — if we change focus we might need clearer focus-visible styles. The current focus ring is 1px and barely visible on light grey backgrounds. Can we make it 3px and match brand blue? jason.prod: strong +1 to clearer focus style. vik.engineering: will try two fixes: 1) ensure virtualizer preserves DOM order, 2) add `aria-posinset`/`aria-setsize`. Also will update CSS: `.alert-row:focus { outline: 3px solid #0066FF; outline-offset: 2px; } /* use focus-visible */` rachel.a11y: also check contrast of that blue against disabled label text — run contrast check. a11y-bot: Automated contrast test — #0066FF on #F7F8FA passes 4.5:1 for 16px body? result: 4.6:1 — okay for normal text. But for 12px captions might fail. emma.design: good catch. For small caption text use darker shade `#004BB5`. amanda.content: I'll update the copy labels to avoid long truncated titles — truncation can hide important info from SR users. Prefer full title in `aria-label` on the row. jason.prod: timeframe? we should target the next sprint for fixes + add a small regression test in e2e keyboard test. vik.engineering: I'll open a PR tomorrow with changes and add NVDA/VoiceOver test steps in the PR description. emma.design: thanks team. If anyone can sanity-check the ARIA attrs in the PR that'd be great. rachel.a11y: will review. Also suggest adding a quick Playwright test: `await page.keyboard.press('Tab')` loop to assert focus lands on each `.alert-row` in order. emma.design: perfect. :thumbsup:
